test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 15 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A metallic sphere of radius 36 cm is dropped into a cylindrical vessel, which is partly filled with water. The diameter of the vessel is 4.8 metres. If the sphere is completely submerged, find by how much the surface of the water will rise.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume displaced = volume of sphere

Rise in water = Volume ÷ Base area of cylinder

r(sphere) = 36 cm ⇒ Volume = (4/3)π × 36³

Radius of cylinder = 4.8/2 = 2.4 m = 240 cm

Height rise = [(4/3)π × 36³] ÷ [π × 240²] = (4 × 36³) ÷ (3 × 240²)

= (4 × 46656) ÷ (3 × 57600) = 186624 ÷ 172800 ≈ 1.08 cm

**∴ Answer ≈ 1.08 cm**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of sphere = 36 cm

Diameter of cylinder = 4.8 m = 480 cm ⇒ radius = 240 cm

**Formula used:**

Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³

Volume of cylinder = πR²h

 
• 
• 

Sphere submerged in cylindrical vessel

**Calculation:**

⇒ Volume of sphere = (4/3)π × 36³ = (4/3)π × 46656

⇒ Let rise in water = h

⇒ Volume displaced = π × 240² × h

⇒ (4/3)π × 46656 = π × 240² × h

⇒ Cancel π

⇒ h = [(4/3) × 46656] ÷ (240²)

⇒ h = 186624 ÷ 172800 ≈ 1.08 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 1.08 cm (approx).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Displacement Principle

Volume of water displaced = volume of immersed object

Cylinder Volume

Volume = Base area × height = πR²h

Unit Conversion

Convert all units into same system before solving

Key Insight

Equate displaced volume with cylinder volume rise
